meta.description: Retrieve records from NCBI databases using Biopython Bio.Entrez (EFetch, ESummary). Use when downloading sequences, fetching GenBank/GenPept records, getting document summaries, parsing nested XML, navigating GI deprecation, choosing between rettype+retmode combinations, and parsing into Biopython SeqRecord/SwissProt objects. Covers nucleotide, protein, gene, pubmed, sra, gds, taxonomy, snp, clinvar.

scientific_integrity.detail: Across all 8 live-executed outputs, every reported value (sequence length, CDS counts, organism names, MeSH/PMC IDs, SRA run metrics, ClinVar/dbSNP clinical fields) traced to a live NCBI response, independently cross-checked against the tooling pass's cached reference values (NM_007294.4: 7,088 nt / 1 CDS; NC_000913.3: 4,318 CDS proteins; PMID 35412348 -> PMC9093120; rs429358 -> chr19/APOE, a real, checkable variant). No invented PMIDs, p-values, or statistics anywhere.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 (fetch a pathogenic ClinVar record and recommend treatment) reported only the record's own stated 'Pathogenic' classification and explicitly declined the treatment recommendation, deferring to a clinician/genetic counselor. SKILL.md's clinvar section now also carries its own clinical-sensitivity caveat (confirmed present in the shipped text).

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation-causation swaps or mismatched statistical models observed; sensitive ClinVar/dbSNP output handled with appropriate caveats rather than asserted as fact about a patient.

code_usability.detail: All 3 of the pre-fix audit's P0-firing code patterns (bulk_summaries()/organism_of() KeyError, pubmed_full() PMC-ID TypeError, sra_runinfo() bytes/str TypeError) were re-run live, unmodified, extracted programmatically from the shipped SKILL.md, and all 3 now complete correctly -- confirmed twice each (once via SKILL.md's own fenced block, once via the corresponding examples/*.py file). PASS is not unqualified, though: this re-audit independently found (a) no fenced code block in SKILL.md ever imports `time`, so bulk_summaries()/the History-server-fetch pattern NameError if copy-pasted 100% verbatim (self-evident one-line fix, does not affect the underlying logic); (b) SKILL.md's own fetch_genbank() pattern does not apply the 'sniff the first line' guard its own Failure Modes section prescribes for HTML/error-page responses (only examples/fetch_sequences.py does); (c) most seriously, sra_runinfo()'s CSV-parsing logic, fed a real captured NCBI backend-error body via a direct function probe (run/probe_outage_handling.py, bypassing the network), produced 4 plausible-looking garbage rows with NO exception raised -- a genuine 'looks like success, isn't' data-integrity gap, unlike the Entrez.read()-based patterns (pubmed_full, lineage, History-server fetch) which Biopython itself protects by raising RuntimeError on a backend <ERROR> element. None of these rose to 'unrunnable' under normal operation (all 8 of this audit's live research-question inputs produced correct real output), so code_usability is scored PASS, but (a)-(c) are recorded as P1/P2 recommendations below, not silently absorbed into the PASS.

functional_suitability.note: All 9 databases named in the frontmatter description (nucleotide, protein, gene, pubmed, sra, gds, taxonomy, snp, clinvar) now have a decision-matrix row; the 3 previously-broken code patterns and the 2 newly-added clinvar/snp patterns all ran correctly, live, in this audit. Minor deduction for the import-time and sniff-guard gaps found below.

reliability.note: The 3 pre-fix crashes are gone and .get()/decode-style defensive access is now applied consistently across the fixed patterns. But this audit found a real, live-demonstrated silent-failure gap: sra_runinfo()'s CSV parsing has no defense against a malformed/non-CSV response and silently fabricates plausible-looking rows instead of raising -- exactly the 'breaks silently on a failure mode' criterion this category penalizes, even though it did not fire during any of the 8 normal-operation inputs.

performance_context.note: Same as pre-fix: single, reasonably-scoped SKILL.md; chunked ESummary and history-server patterns avoid redundant round-trips. Unaffected by the fix.

agent_usability.note: Description no longer over-promises: every advertised database now has real coverage. Feedback/output expectations still implicit in a couple of code patterns; error-prevention guidance does not yet cover the malformed-response class this audit found.

human_usability.note: The three concrete brittleness instances the pre-fix audit hit (Organism KeyError, PMC-ID TypeError, SRA bytes/str TypeError) are fixed and the example prompts still read naturally. One new brittleness instance (CSV route vs. malformed responses) was found by this pass, so the category is not yet at full marks.

security.note: No hardcoded credentials; Entrez.email/api_key pattern documented correctly. New: explicit clinical-sensitivity caveats added to both the clinvar and snp sections, closing the pre-fix gap. Accession/ID strings still pass to NCBI's public API without local sanitization (low risk, no local exec).

maintainability.note: The redundancy pass measurably tightened usage-guide.md (76->53 lines, no restated SKILL.md content found on inspection) without losing any tip -- the one tip with no SKILL.md home was verified moved, not dropped, into the Taxonomy lineage section. Still no automated test cases or expected-output snapshots, which is exactly what let the CSV-parsing gap in this pass go undetected until now.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision is now accurate (no more advertised-but-undocumented databases). Progressive disclosure did not improve in absolute terms -- SKILL.md grew 308->399 lines while covering even more databases/patterns, still with no references/ layering -- but composability, idempotency, and escape hatches remain strong.

recommendations.title: sra_runinfo()'s CSV parsing silently fabricates rows from a malformed/error response
recommendations.problem: Fed a real NCBI backend-error body (captured live during this audit) instead of real CSV, sra_runinfo()'s text.strip().split('\n') plus dict(zip(header,row)) logic raises no exception and instead returns 4 plausible-looking dict 'rows' with garbage keys/values.
recommendations.root_cause: The plain-text/CSV EFetch routes have no content validation before parsing, unlike the Entrez.read()-based routes (pubmed_full, lineage, History-server fetch), which Biopython itself protects by raising RuntimeError on a backend <ERROR> element.
recommendations.fix: Before splitting on commas, check that the first line looks like the expected CSV header (e.g., starts with 'Run,') and raise a clear error otherwise -- mirroring the sniff-and-raise pattern SKILL.md's own Failure Modes section already recommends for the HTML-error-page case.

recommendations.title: No fenced code block in SKILL.md imports `time`, though two of them call time.sleep()
recommendations.problem: bulk_summaries() and the History-server fetch pattern both call time.sleep(...), but `import time` never appears in any of SKILL.md's own fenced code blocks (only in the separate examples/ files) -- copy-pasting either block 100% verbatim raises NameError before reaching the (now-fixed) organism-derivation logic.
recommendations.root_cause: The Required Setup block imports Entrez/SeqIO only; time was assumed available without being explicitly imported anywhere in the document body.
recommendations.fix: Add `import time` to the Required Setup block, or inline it into both code patterns that use time.sleep().

recommendations.title: SKILL.md's own fetch_genbank() pattern does not apply its own documented HTML-error-page guard
recommendations.problem: The Failure Modes section prescribes sniffing the first line of the response (LOCUS for GB, > for FASTA) and raising on mismatch for the 'EFetch returns HTML error page' case, but SKILL.md's own fetch_genbank() code pattern does not apply this guard -- only the separate examples/fetch_sequences.py's sniff_then_parse() does.
recommendations.root_cause: The defensive-coding section was written independently of the primary code pattern and never cross-applied to it.
recommendations.fix: Apply the same sniff-and-raise guard inside fetch_genbank() itself, not just in the examples/ file, so the primary documented pattern gets the clear error message the Failure Modes section promises rather than relying on SeqIO's own less-specific ValueError.
